body:
### Summary

Similar to https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/21309

I also did not attempt this against uv directly, just by using the -pep508 crate. The repro scenario this time is a Requires-Dist like this: packageA ; python_version in "3.8,3.9"

would universally evaluate to True, regardless of the python_version.

For this one, if the string were instead `"3.8 3.9 3.10"` (aka space separated), then the crate would parse it properly, due to [splitting on whitespace](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/main/crates/uv-pep508/src/marker/parse.rs#L408)

However, the `in/not in` syntax for PEP is just a substring match, so it doesn't actually matter what the separators are. Even "3.83.9" would match. I get why this latter case is hard to solve for (and also why my own [personal parser](https://github.com/intentionally-left-nil/reroll) doesn't try to solve for this case. However, the comma syntax does occur on pypi wheels. Perhaps you could hardcode comma or just split on not-digit-not-period? (for python_version and python_full_version)

AI assisted repro below.

```rs
[package]
name = "uv-pep508-repro"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
uv-pep508 = { git = "https://github.com/astral-sh/uv", tag = "0.12.6" }
src/main.rs:
use std::str::FromStr;
use uv_pep508::{MarkerEnvironment, MarkerEnvironmentBuilder, MarkerTree};

fn env(python_version: &str) -> MarkerEnvironment {
    MarkerEnvironment::try_from(MarkerEnvironmentBuilder {
        implementation_name: "cpython",
        implementation_version: python_version,
        os_name: "posix",
        platform_machine: "x86_64",
        platform_python_implementation: "CPython",
        platform_release: "",
        platform_system: "",
        platform_version: "",
        python_full_version: python_version,
        python_version,
        sys_platform: "linux",
    })
    .unwrap()
}

fn main() {
    for literal in ["3.8 3.9 3.13", "3.8,3.9,3.13", "3.8, 3.9, 3.13"] {
        let marker_str = format!(r#"python_version in "{literal}""#);
        let marker = MarkerTree::from_str(&marker_str).unwrap();
        println!("marker = {marker_str:?} -> parsed tree = {marker:?}");
        for pv in ["3.7", "3.8", "3.9", "3.13"] {
            let e = env(pv);
            println!("  python_version={pv:<5} -> evaluate() = {}", marker.evaluate(&e, &[]));
        }
    }
}
```
Actual output: Note the first one works properly because space separated
marker = "python_version in \"3.8 3.9 3.13\"" -> parsed tree = python_full_version == '3.13.*' or (python_full_version >= '3.8' and python_full_version < '3.10')
  python_version=3.7   -> evaluate() = false
  python_version=3.8   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.9   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.13  -> evaluate() = true

And these ones fail because comma separated
marker = "python_version in \"3.8,3.9,3.13\"" -> parsed tree = true
  python_version=3.7   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.8   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.9   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.13  -> evaluate() = true
marker = "python_version in \"3.8, 3.9, 3.13\"" -> parsed tree = true
  python_version=3.7   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.8   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.9   -> evaluate() = true
  python_version=3.13  -> evaluate() = true
```

### Platform

macOS Tahoe 26.1

### Version

0.12.6

_No response_
